newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up but volumes thin.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up but volumes thin.

text.p: Gold in Hong Kong ended slightly up on Monday from its previous New York close on light Japanese buying and physical bargain-hunting, but gold dealers said traded volumes were dismal.
"Things are pretty quiet with the U.S. market holiday," said a bullion chief at a local bank.
U.S. markets were closed on Monday for the Veteran's Day holiday.
Only small amounts of buying from traders on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange were reported following minor dollar/yen movements.
Gold was expected to trade between US$377 and $382, with short covering anticipated at the lower end of the range and fresh short positions established towards the top end, some dealers said.
Some traders expected an increase in open interest on COMEX, projecting more short positions.
Bullion ended at $379.70/380.20 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$379.20/70 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$4 higher at HK$3,499 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.50 from its previous fix at -4.50.
